question: Cholesterol from the liver is transpoed to the peripheral tissue mainly by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cholesterol is synthesized in the liver" -> "Cholesterol needs to be transported to peripheral tissues" -> "LDL is the primary carrier of cholesterol in the bloodstream" -> "LDL delivers cholesterol to peripheral tissues" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Liver produces cholesterol" -> "Cholesterol is packaged into lipoproteins" -> "LDL is formed from VLDL after triglyceride removal" -> "LDL primarily transports cholesterol to tissues" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Cholesterol is produced in the liver" -> "Cholesterol is transported via lipoproteins" -> "VLDL primarily carries triglycerides" -> "LDL is the main transporter of cholesterol" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Cholesterol is synthesized in the liver" -> "Cholesterol is released into the bloodstream" -> "Chylomicrons transport dietary lipids" -> "LDL is responsible for cholesterol transport to tissues" -> 80%
analysis: Cholesterol is primarily transported from the liver to peripheral tissues by Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL). LDL is responsible for delivering cholesterol to cells throughout the body, which is essential for various cellular functions and membrane integrity.
